questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.**

If he __tried__ he would have succeeded.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** 'had tried'**

__
 
• There are three forms of conditional sentences :
 
• **Conditional 1:** ‘if+simple present, will future E.g.* If I find her address, I’ll send her an invitation.*
 
• ***Conditional 2:** ‘if+simple past, conditional 1' **(=would+infinitive) **E.g. If I found her address, I would send her an invitation.*
 
• ***Conditional 3:** ‘if+past perfect, conditional 2' **(=would+have+past participle) ** E.g. If I had found her address, I would have sent her an invitation.*

This is a **third** conditional sentence showing a condition that is possible to achieve, and so it has to be written in the same format. Thus **option 3 is the most suitable option** and it should be written as ***'If he had tried he would have__ succeeded.'***

questions.question: Side of a square is first increased by 10% and then decreased by 20%. What is the overall percentage change in area?

questions.question: Which of the following statements about the Lok Sabha is NOT correct?

options.text: A money bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha
No-confidence motion against the Council of Ministers can only be moved in Lok Sabha
The Union Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the Lok Sabha
If the question arises whether a bill is a money bill or not, the decision of the leader of the opposition shall be final

questions.solution:
Option **4** is correct, i.e. If the question arises whether a bill is a money bill or not, the decision of the leader of the opposition shall be final.

 
• **Lok Sabha Speaker certifies** the bill as **a money bill** before sending it to the upper house, and the decision of the Speaker is binding on both the Houses.He/she represents the full authority of the House and decides whether a bill is a money bill or not.
 
• A money bill or supply bill is a bill that solely concerns taxation or government spending.
 
• The Speaker appoints the Secretary-General of the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Lok Sabha speaker is the presiding officer of the Lok Sabha.
 
• The Speaker ranks sixth in the hierarchy of State government of India, equivalent with the Chief Justice.
 
• Money bills are defined in** Article 110** of the Indian Constitution. Special procedure regarding Money Bills is contained in Article 109.
 
• The Upper House of the Parliament i.e. the Rajya Sabha does not have the right to amend the Money bills. It can only recommend amendments.
 
• The Annual Financial (Budget) bills and the Appropriation bills are termed as the Money bills.
